name: Cryolipolysis (CoolSculpting Mini Chin)

card.summary: Fat freezing under the chin: a cleared non-surgical option with modest measured fat reduction and a rare paradoxical-growth side effect.
card.note: Reviews rate data quality as low; rare paradoxical adipose hyperplasia (enlargement of treated fat) has been reported.

quick.overview:
Cryolipolysis is a non-invasive procedure that uses controlled cold to reduce small pockets of fat. Under the chin (the submental area, often called a double chin) it is one of the treatment sites cleared by the US FDA, and a smaller applicator is sometimes marketed as a mini-chin treatment.

In looksmaxxing discussions it is raised as a non-surgical way to sharpen the jaw-neck line. Systematic reviews report modest average reductions in fat thickness, and the evidence base is described by reviewers as low in quality.
quick.mechanism: A device cools the skin and underlying subcutaneous fat over a set period. Cold is intended to damage fat tissue in the treated area, which the body then gradually clears. Reviews measure the result as skinfold or ultrasound fat-thickness change over following months.
quick.risks: Commonly reported effects are redness, numbness, swelling, bruising and mild pain, usually resolving within weeks. A rare effect, paradoxical adipose hyperplasia, in which the treated fat enlarges, is reported at roughly 0.12% to 1.0% depending on the study, and surgical options such as liposuction are described for treating it.

lead: Cryolipolysis, commonly called fat freezing and sold under the CoolSculpting brand, is a non-invasive procedure that applies controlled cold to the skin to reduce subcutaneous fat in targeted areas.[1] Under the chin it is used to shrink a submental fat pad, the soft fullness often called a double chin, so the jaw-neck line looks sharper and the lower face more defined. The US FDA has cleared the technique for the submental area, along with the jawline, arms, flanks, abdomen and thighs.[1]

In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a non-surgical route to a more defined jaw-neck angle, sometimes under the label mini chin, referring to a smaller applicator used for the chin area. People weigh it against alternatives such as deoxycholic acid injections, radiofrequency devices and liposuction; one review of non-surgical neck treatments lists cryolipolysis among the options for submental fat.[5]

Systematic reviews of cryolipolysis across body areas report average fat-thickness reductions and high patient satisfaction, while reviewers rate the quality of the data as low.[1][3] A 2025 meta-analysis of 30 studies found reductions in circumference and fat thickness at 12 weeks, with adverse events commonly reported but mostly mild.[4]

paras: The procedure applies controlled cooling to a fold of skin and fat for a set session. It is performed in a clinic without incisions or anesthesia, and is marketed to people with small, localized fat deposits rather than as a weight-loss method [1].

Zeltiq Aesthetics developed the technology and introduced it in the United States in 2010 under the CoolSculpting name. Allergan Aesthetics acquired Zeltiq in 2017, with the acquisition reported as completed on April 28, 2017 [1].

A 2015 systematic review of 19 studies reported average skinfold-thickness reductions between about 10% and 28.5%, with high satisfaction among patients [1]. A 2023 review of 18 studies reported average ultrasound-measured fat-thickness reductions of 2.0 to 5.1 mm and concluded the procedure appears safe and modestly effective, while rating the quality of the underlying data as low [1].

A 2023 review in the Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology describes the mechanism as cold-induced apoptosis of fat cells, with clearance by macrophages, and reports significant fat-volume reduction and high patient satisfaction while calling for more research in different treatment areas.[10]
Commonly reported effects are redness, numbness, swelling, bruising and mild pain, which usually resolve within weeks [1].

Paradoxical adipose hyperplasia, in which the treated fat grows instead of shrinking, is reported as rare, with published rates ranging from 0.12% to 1.0% depending on the study. Described treatments include liposuction or abdominoplasty [1].

sections.h: Use for the chin and in looksmaxxing communities
paras: A review of non-surgical neck rejuvenation lists percutaneous radiofrequency, radiofrequency-helium plasma, deoxycholic acid injections and cryolipolysis as options for submental preplatysmal fat, and reports percutaneous radiofrequency as having the highest patient satisfaction and lowest complication rate among them.[5] A review of male body contouring notes that men increasingly request body contouring and that cryolipolysis is among the non-invasive devices used, alongside invasive options such as liposuction and jawline fillers.[6]

On looksmax.org, an early thread presented fat freezing as a slower non-invasive form of liposuction and speculated about using it on cheek fat; a user in another thread asked about chin treatment as a man under 30 and noted most online examples are middle-aged women.[7][8] A T Nation member who received two sessions on the love handles reported a visible difference but felt the area returned to its earlier look after a few months.[9]

Reviews of cryolipolysis across body areas are summarized above [1]. A small trial of fat reduction in the submandibular and submental area (14 participants, started February 2016) is registered as completed on ClinicalTrials.gov; no results are given in the registration record available here [2].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, fat freezing is discussed as a local fat-loss option for the chin and face, with posters asking whether it works for men under 30 and for cheek fat.[7][8]

claims.claim: Freezing fat gives permanent local fat loss under the chin
claims.believers: Posters describe it as a slower non-invasive liposuction that removes fat in stubborn pockets such as the submental area.[7][8]
claims.experts: Reviews report average fat-thickness reductions of a few millimetres with high satisfaction, and rate the data quality as low.[1][3]

claims.claim: Cold exposure converts white fat to burning brown fat in the treated area
claims.believers: A looksmax.org post proposes that freezing induces white fat cells to become brown fat cells that burn calories to produce heat.[7]
claims.experts: Reviews describe the main mechanism as cold-induced apoptosis of fat cells followed by clearance by macrophages.[1]

claims.believers: A poster asked and a reply said it should reduce any fat tissue in the cheeks, including stubborn pockets.[7]
claims.experts: Cleared sites listed on Wikipedia include the submental area, jawline and body areas; the cheeks are not among the sites listed.[1]

Body gradually clears them over following months
Less submental fullness and a crisper jaw-neck line
angle.text: The treatment thins the fat sitting under the chin, which is the part of a double chin that weight loss alone may leave behind. People use it to define the jawline and neck angle without surgery.
